How to launch:

Upon liftoff keep your thrust at 150 mps. If you go any higher than that you will be fighting the gravity of Kerbin and wasting fuel. You can increase to full thrust once your vehicle has reached maximum dynamic pressure, which on Kerbin is 10,000 meters. At that point you also want to begin your gravity turn. Tilt your spacecraft by 45 degrees in the direction of the apoapsis and maintain your thrust until your trajectory reaches an altitude above 70,000 meters. That marks the edge of the planer's atmosphere. Anything beyond that is vacuum. As you reach the height of your trajectory tilt the craft so that it points directly at the apoapsis and apply max thrust until your periapsis has an altitude above 70,000 meters. Upon doing that you will have successfully achieved orbit.

To get to orbit efficiently you want to be about 300 km/s, a bit lower than 45 degrees, and at the top of the thickest part of the atmosphere at about the same time. So gradually tip over and slowly reduce your throttle until you're in thinner air.

At about 55,000 meters you want to be aiming horizontal (if you have enough thrust not to fall back) and already be halfway to orbit (you want the line that shows where you're going to be nearly halfway around the planet)

You want your middle stage (upper Kerbin atmosphere) to have a thrust ratio of at least 1 until you're more experienced.

The most efficient thrust ration is about 2, but anything over 1.5 is okay. Over 3 and you're overpowered and could probably save weight with a smaller engine (or you may want to reduce your boosters thrust)

The fuel cells are worthless for even going to the Mun since they never shut off. You'll want to build tech on the electricity side (bottom of the tech tree) until you can get solar panels.

If you're landing on the Mun the first time you probably want a wide lander for more stability.

Don't forget your parachute. Don't forget your solar panels. Don't forget your landing legs.

To align with another planet look at the dotted line labeled an or the opposite one labeled dn. Those stand for ascending and descending node. Line your view up so you're looking straight down that line. Then plan a maneuver at precisely that point such that it brings the path of your craft into the orbit that matches the path of your target.

To mate two vessels in orbit: Match the orbital plane, (the thing I talked about just above) (make sure they're orbiting the same direction) put one vessel into a higher orbit than the other, (not absolutely necessary but it makes it much easier and faster) and plan a maneuver node to bring them as close together as you can get. (you'll get better with practice.) When they're close, click the icon you use to stabilize the craft. If it changes to "target" instead of "orbit" you're close enough. Repeatedly burn retrograde (in this mode it reduces your speed relative to the target, not the planet) and then toward the target until you're close.

When you can see your target in the regular view (not in map mode) aim at the target and cut your thrust to 2-5%. Do a very gentle burn straight at the target. Right click on the target's docking port and click "set as target". Then hit the button to aim at the target. Then switch to operating your target vessel using the [ key. On your target vessel again right click on the docking port you want to aim up and click "set as target" and the button to aim that at the target. Switch back and forth, repeatedly telling each ship to align with the other's docking port. When it's well aligned approach at about 2 meters per second until they attach. If you have RCS you can hit the docking mode button, hit R to turn on rcs, and use the ikjl keys to precisely match up as you approach.
